videos.title: Enthalpy, Entropy and Non-Equilibrium Reactions | Year 12 Chemistry
videos.description:
Explain why burning glucose and photosynthesis stay away from equilibrium, using the signs of the enthalpy change and the entropy change. Read the sign of the Gibbs free energy change (delta G) to decide whether a reaction is favoured, and keep that separate from how fast it runs. Work through the glucose example one step at a time, then compare the reverse process, photosynthesis.

Chemistry 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Equilibrium and Acid Reactions. Supports analysing non-equilibrium systems in terms of the effect of entropy and enthalpy.
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Chemistry Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"analyse examples of non-equilibrium systems in terms of the effect of entropy and enthalpy, for example:
- combustion reactions
- photosynthesis"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/chemistry-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Dynamic equilibrium in a closed system, exothermic and endothermic reactions, entropy as the spread of particles and energy, and the link between enthalpy, entropy and delta G. Next: What a flask already at equilibrium does when it is disturbed by a change in concentration or temperature.

#Year12Chemistry #Entropy #HSCScience
syllabusDotpoints:
analyse examples of non-equilibrium systems in terms of the effect of entropy and enthalpy, for example:
- combustion reactions
- photosynthesis

videos.title: Squeezing a Gas Equilibrium: Predicting the Shift | Year 12 Chemistry
videos.description:
Squeeze a gas mixture that is sitting at equilibrium and predict which way it shifts by counting only the gas particles. Explain the shift as the side with fewer gas particles becoming favoured when every gas is more crowded. Handle equal gas counts and solids, and tell a squeeze apart from adding an inert gas at fixed volume.

Chemistry 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Equilibrium and Acid Reactions. Supports explaining how pressure and volume changes affect an equilibrium, using Le Chatelier’s principle and collision theory.
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Chemistry Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"investigate the effects of temperature, concentration, volume and/or pressure on a system at equilibrium and explain how Le Chatelier’s principle can be used to predict such effects"
"explain the overall observations about equilibrium in terms of the collision theory"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/chemistry-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Le Chatelier’s principle for concentration and temperature changes, why a disturbance is only partly cancelled, and gas pressure as particles hitting the walls (Year 11). Next: Catalysts and equilibrium, a faster route to the same mixture.

#Year12Chemistry #Equilibrium #HSCScience
syllabusDotpoints: investigate the effects of temperature, concentration, volume and/or pressure on a system at equilibrium and explain how Le Chatelier’s principle can be used to predict such effects

videos.title: Flowering Plant Reproduction: Pollination to Seed | Year 12 Biology
videos.description:
Sequence reproduction in flowering plants from pollination to seed, and explain why pollination is not yet fertilisation. Explain how a pollen tube carries sperm to the egg. Name vegetative propagation as the asexual route in plants, then match each route to the conditions where it works best.

Biology 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Heredity. Supports analysing sexual and asexual reproduction in plants.
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Biology Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"explain the mechanisms of reproduction that ensure the continuity of a species, by analysing sexual and asexual methods of reproduction in a variety of organisms, including but not limited to:
- plants: asexual and sexual reproduction"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/biology-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Sexual and asexual reproduction, gametes joining at fertilisation, clones, and the conditions that favour clones or variety. Next: Reproduction without flowers or seeds: yeast, bacteria and protists.

#Year12Biology #Reproduction #HSCScience
syllabusDotpoints:
explain the mechanisms of reproduction that ensure the continuity of a species, by analysing sexual and asexual methods of reproduction in a variety of organisms, including but not limited to:
- plants: asexual and sexual reproduction

videos.title: How DNA Is Copied: Base Pairing and Replication | Year 12 Biology
videos.description:
Explain how a cell copies billions of DNA letters almost without error. Name the parts of a DNA nucleotide, pair A with T and C with G, and explain why one strand acts as a template for the other. Trace a short molecule through semi-conservative replication, where each new molecule keeps one original strand, and explain why copying errors are rare.

Biology 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Heredity. Supports modelling DNA replication using the Watson and Crick model, including nucleotide composition, pairing and bonding.
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Biology Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"model the processes involved in cell replication, including but not limited to:
- DNA replication using the Watson and Crick DNA model, including nucleotide composition, pairing and bonding"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/biology-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: DNA as inherited information, genes, alleles and copying errors, and how a single cell copies its DNA before it splits. Next: Mitosis, how a cell shares its copied chromosomes between two new cells.

#Year12Biology #DNA #HSCScience
syllabusDotpoints:
model the processes involved in cell replication, including but not limited to:
- DNA replication using the Watson and Crick DNA model, including nucleotide composition, pairing and bonding

videos.title: Human Pregnancy: Fertilisation to Implantation | Year 12 Biology
videos.description:
Trace a human pregnancy from fertilisation in the oviduct, through cleavage and the blastocyst, to implantation in a uterine lining that progesterone has prepared. Explain why the embryo’s hCG keeps the corpus luteum making progesterone, and why the placenta takes over progesterone over the first two to three months. Separate hCG from progesterone, and an embryo from a fetus.

Biology 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Heredity. Supports analysing fertilisation, implantation and the hormonal control of pregnancy in mammals.
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Biology Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"analyse the features of fertilisation, implantation and hormonal control of pregnancy and birth in mammals"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/biology-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Sexual reproduction in animals, one set of chromosomes in each gamete, and internal fertilisation with few young. Next: How pregnancy hormone loops hold a pregnancy steady, and how labour builds.

#Year12Biology #Pregnancy #HSCScience
syllabusDotpoints: analyse the features of fertilisation, implantation and hormonal control of pregnancy and birth in mammals

videos.title: Pregnancy Feedback and Labour: Hormone Loops | Year 12 Biology
videos.description:
Explain how a pregnancy stays steady for nine months, and why no new egg is released during it. Use negative feedback, where progesterone turns down the pituitary hormones FSH and LH, to explain why ovulation stops. Explain how labour builds through positive feedback involving oxytocin and the cervix, and how prolactin and oxytocin help make and release milk.

Biology 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Heredity. Supports analysing the hormonal control of pregnancy and birth in mammals, including negative and positive feedback.
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Biology Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"analyse the features of fertilisation, implantation and hormonal control of pregnancy and birth in mammals"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/biology-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Human pregnancy from fertilisation to implantation, including hCG, progesterone and the placenta, and that a hormone is a messenger carried by the blood. Next: How farmers use reproduction knowledge to breed animals and crops.

#Year12Biology #Pregnancy #HSCScience
syllabusDotpoints: analyse the features of fertilisation, implantation and hormonal control of pregnancy and birth in mammals

videos.title: The Equilibrium Constant, K: Writing Expressions | Year 12 Chemistry
videos.description:
When a settled mixture changes all of its amounts, the ratio of concentrations stays the same at a fixed temperature. Name that ratio K and write its expression for a reaction in solution from a balanced equation, using coefficients as powers and leaving out solids and pure liquids. Read whether a stated K is large, small or middling for that reaction.

Chemistry 2017: Year 12 Module 5, Equilibrium and Acid Reactions. Supports deducing equilibrium expressions for homogeneous reactions in solution.
Syllabus dotpoint (NSW Chemistry Stage 6, 2017, Module 5):
"deduce the equilibrium expression (in terms of Keq) for homogeneous reactions occurring in solution"
Official 2017 course: https://www.nsw.gov.au/education-and-training/nesa/curriculum/science/chemistry-stage-6-2017

Prerequisite: Dynamic equilibrium with equal non-zero rates, the settled mixtures from the earlier flask and tube examples, and concentration as moles per litre. Next: Calculating K and equilibrium concentrations with an ICE table.

#Year12Chemistry #Keq #HSCScience
syllabusDotpoints: deduce the equilibrium expression (in terms of Keq) for homogeneous reactions occurring in solution
